transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’ve had this thing going on for a while, and it’s hard to explain without sounding like I’m making it bigger than it is.

I work in finance, and I’m around a lot of events in Cincinnati—networking stuff, panels, arts fundraisers sometimes, you know, the kind of places where everyone sort of knows everyone. And I’ve been pretty convinced that certain people in those arts and finance circles are keeping track of which clients I’m meeting with. Not openly, exactly, but quietly.

It’s like… invitations show up with certain wording, or a panel topic seems a little too related to something I just discussed, or someone sits near me at an event and it feels arranged. And I know, I can tell myself, “Okay, maybe that’s just coincidence,” because Cincinnati can be small that way—my bachelor’s program was like that too, everyone connected to everyone—but I can’t really let it go. It keeps sticking in my head, and that’s why I thought I should come talk to someone.

When you notice these things—like the wording of an invitation or someone sitting near you—how convinced are you, on a scale from 'it's just a nagging thought I can't shake' to 'I'm certain this is really happening,' that people are actually tracking your meetings?

I’d say it’s more than just a nagging thought. I’m not, like, 100 percent saying I could prove it in court or anything, but in the moment it feels pretty convincing.

Like with the invitations, it’s not just the words—it’s the timing, and then a panel topic will be close to something I just talked about with a client, and then someone from the same circle ends up sitting near me. And Cincinnati’s small, you know, especially if you’ve been around finance and arts events, people overlap all the time. I remember even in my bachelor’s program, there were these little networks where everybody knew somebody, so part of me says maybe that’s all it is.

But… I keep coming back to the feeling that certain people are quietly tracking who I meet with and sending little signals about it. I can try to talk myself out of it, but it doesn’t really loosen its grip.

How long has this feeling that people are tracking your meetings been going on—did it start fairly recently, or has this kind of suspicious thinking about others been part of how you've generally seen people since you were younger?

It hasn’t been, like, since I was a kid or anything. I mean, I’ve always been aware that people talk—especially in finance, and Cincinnati can feel like one big hallway sometimes—but this specific thing, with people tracking my client meetings and the invitations or little signals… that’s been about two months.

I remember because it kind of started around a stretch of events I was going to, and then I kept noticing patterns. But yeah, roughly two months.
Besides these suspicions about being tracked, have you noticed anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or sounds other people don't seem to hear, or seeing things that others don't see?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the way you mean, like hearing a voice talking to me or seeing something that isn’t there.

Sometimes at events I’ll hear my name and turn, but that happens in crowded rooms, right? Like there’s music and people talking over each other, and the acoustics in those old Cincinnati venues are weird—some fundraiser spaces are all marble and glass, so everything bounces around. But I wouldn’t say I’m hearing voices other people can’t hear, no.

Seeing things… no, I haven’t noticed anything like that. It’s more about the patterns and timing of things than, like, my senses doing something strange.

Over these past two months, has this feeling that people are tracking you been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches of days or weeks where it went away completely and then came back?

It’s been… about two months overall, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m sitting there every minute thinking about it, because I still go to work and do normal things, and sometimes I get distracted.

But the belief itself hasn’t really gone away completely for, like, a week or something. It’s more that it fades into the background and then something happens—an invitation, a seating thing, someone mentioning a client-adjacent topic—and it comes right back. Cincinnati is funny that way, too, because you run into the same names and circles over and over, so it’s hard to separate what’s coincidence from what’s… not.

So, yeah, about two months, on and off in intensity, but not gone completely.
Was there a particular stressful event, life change, or crisis happening around two months ago when these suspicions first started?

I’m not sure there was one big thing. Like, not a crisis where I can point to it and say, “That’s when everything changed.”

Around that time I was going to more events, more client-adjacent things, and those can get stressful in their own way—keeping track of who knows who, who’s talking to whom. But that’s kind of normal for my work too. Finance is… it’s a lot of small conversations that don’t seem important until later, and then you think back and go, wait, why did that person bring that up?

So, I don’t know. I can’t think of a specific life change. It just sort of built up around then.

Aside from this belief about being tracked, how would you say your day-to-day functioning has been—are you still handling your work performance, sleep, and relationships normally, or has this affected those areas significantly?

I mean… I’m still working. I don’t want to give the impression that I’ve fallen apart or anything. I still see clients, I still answer emails, I still go into the office.

But if I’m being honest, my practice has gotten smaller than it was. Some of that is just the market too—people get cautious, they don’t always want to schedule reviews, and Cincinnati can be very relationship-based, like if you miss one breakfast or one golf outing, suddenly you’re not in the loop.

But… yeah, I’ve been missing follow-ups more than I used to. Or I’ll put off calling someone back because I’m not sure where the information is going to end up. And I’ve avoided a couple of public panels or networking things, which I normally would’ve done without thinking. So I’m still functioning, but I’m not keeping the same level of client contact that I used to manage.

I mean, I think I mostly said it… I’m still doing the basics. I get up, I go to work, I deal with people. It’s not like everything stopped.

It’s just hard to measure what “normal” is, because in my line of work things can slow down for reasons that have nothing to do with me. Clients get busy, markets get weird, people say they’ll circle back and then they don’t. And Cincinnati has this thing where business and social stuff blur together, so if you skip something, you don’t always know if it matters or not.

So… I’d say I’m functioning, but maybe not as smoothly as before. I don’t know if I’d call it significant, exactly. It’s noticeable to me.
Have you noticed any changes in how you speak or organize your thoughts, or any unusual behaviors that others have commented on, during this period?

I don’t think so… not in a way people have said to me directly. I mean, sometimes I lose my train of thought, but everybody does that, especially when you’re juggling client stuff and market updates and whatever headline people are panicking about that week.

My sister did say I sounded “all over the place” once on the phone, but she says that when I talk about work anyway, because she doesn’t follow finance, so to her anything with yields or estate planning or client referrals sounds like a maze. And honestly, half the time the conversations at work are like that too—one person mentions a municipal bond issue, then suddenly you’re talking about someone’s kid going to Xavier, and then it circles back to a client dinner.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had unusual behavior people are pointing out. Maybe I’ve been a little more distracted, but nobody has sat me down or anything.
